audits.mathematicalReason: For two nonoverlapping circles of radii a and b tangent to the floor and to each other, the horizontal center separation is sqrt((a+b)^2-(a-b)^2)=2sqrt(ab). Thus the original centers have horizontal separation 1. If the third radius is r and t=sqrt(r)>0, its horizontal separations from the radius-1 and radius-1/4 centers are 2t and t. A center between them gives 2t+t=1, so r=1/9; a center beyond the smaller circle gives 2t-t=1, so r=1. A center left of the larger circle cannot satisfy the separations. Alternatively, place the original centers at (0,1) and (1,1/4), and the third at (x,r). Tangency gives x^2=4r and (x-1)^2=r, reducing to (9r-1)(r-1)=0. Both positive roots satisfy the original tangency equations. The two routes are valid alternatives, not jointly required methods.

figureEvidence.fact: The head-on view shows the larger circle to the left of the smaller circle, with both above and tangent to the same horizontal floor and externally tangent to one another. Their interiors do not overlap.

audits.mathematicalReason: Two distinct lattice points on a nonvertical line force its slope to be a quotient of integers. Conversely, if a rational-slope line of slope p/q contains a lattice point (a,b), then it contains (a+kq,b+kp) for every integer k, so it contains infinitely many. Rational-slope lines can also contain no lattice points: y=(p/q)x+1/(2q) is an example. Consequently, both zero-slope and nonzero-rational-slope rows allow only zero and more than two. An irrational-slope line has at most one lattice point; y=mx contains exactly one, while y=mx+1/2 contains none. Its row therefore allows zero and exactly one. The rows each have two Possible entries, totaling six. The slope formula and rational/irrational distinction are directly supported by their supplied scopes.

audits.mathematicalReason: Each block is (1/2)/10=1/20 mile long. After five blocks, five minutes remain before the usual arrival time. Replacing one of the five remaining blocks by three increases the remaining distance to seven blocks, or 7/20 mile. Five minutes is 1/12 hour, so the required speed is (7/20)/(1/12)=4.2 miles per hour. The distance-speed-time relationship and time-unit conversion are both defensible assessed scopes.
